sources.title: Government says proposed cyber law will not muzzle press freedom

quotes.text: DHAKA, Sept 10, 2026 (BSS) - Information and Broadcasting Minister Andaleeve Rahman today said the government has no intention of suppressing free thought, freedom of the press or journalists through the proposed Cyber Security (Amendment) Act, 2026.
The draft law is being revised with great care so that it does not contain any ambiguous (dual-meaning) words that could create opportunities for misuse against the media in the future,
Provisions for punishment of false complainants and the removal of non-bailable provisions are commendable, he stated.

sources.title: Government moves to amend Cyber Security Act

quotes.text: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed yesterday told parliament that the government has started the process to amend the Cyber Security Act to curb the spread of rumors, misinformation, defamatory content, and AI‑generated deceptive images, videos, and audio on social media.
He said the revised law will also include provisions to compel international technology platforms, including Meta (Facebook’s parent company), to remove harmful content within a specified timeframe.

quotes.text: A major deficiency of the draft CPO is that the same law seeks to regulate both cybercrimes (e.g. hacking) and online content (e.g. gendered harassment), although the two issues are fundamentally different in nature and require different approaches and solutions.
All provisions related to content removal and blocking of information should be clearly defined by law and fully in line with international human rights standards.
